@about: CabinetCraft add-on for PartCraft (0.8 DC.117). Words of the add-on only. Part, material and hardware names are keys written into the job's cut list. Placeholder cost wording follows rule EG.76.
name: CabinetCraft
job.intro: A job is a room with runs of cabinets along its walls. Pick the unit and how the cabinets are built, give the room's size, then lay out the runs in the Layout view.
job.name: Job name
job.room.note: The room's height. Its shape, walls, doors and windows are set in the Room view.
job.kept: The job is kept in this browser as you work. Save the job file to keep it anywhere else.
run.none: This job has no run yet. Add one with the Run button.
run.title: First machine run
run.name: Name
run.autofill: Fill a small leftover (up to 75 mm or 3 in) with a filler
row.base: Floor row: base, drawer and tall cabinets
row.over: Over the wall by {n} {unit}: take a cabinet out or make one narrower.
add.fill.title: Add a filler for what is left, when it is 75 mm (3 in) or less
tpl.wall-over: Wall, over the fridge or hood
mat.intro: Pick the board, the back, the fronts and the edge banding. The names and thicknesses go into the cut list; the sheet size of each is the nest's.
mat.rules.note: Common shop practice in numbers you can change. Check them against your hardware before cutting.
rule.shelfFront: Shelf set back from the front ({unit})
mat.custom.note: Add a board your shop buys. The thickness and sheet size are in {unit}. Its name stays as you type it.
mat.custom.name: Name
checks.count: {n} to look at, {e} of them errors.
checks.none: Nothing to fix: no cabinet or run has a problem that the checks can see.
checks.shared: The same list is in the Problems panel.
prob.cab.too-narrow: {no} is too narrow for its two sides: it needs more than {min} {unit}.
prob.cab.too-low: {no} is too low for its panels: it needs more than {min} {unit}.
prob.cab.too-shallow: {no} is too shallow for its back and shelves: it needs more than {min} {unit}.
prob.cab.no-slide: {no} has no drawer slide that fits its depth: it needs at least {min} {unit} deep.
prob.cab.drawer-low: {no} has a drawer front too low for a drawer box: each needs at least {min} {unit}.
prob.cab.fronts-tall: {no} has drawer fronts adding up to {sum} {unit}, more than the {max} {unit} it has.
prob.cab.door-wide: {no} has a door {w} wide; most shops keep a single door to {max} or less.
prob.blind.short: {no} has a blind part of {blind}; it should be at least {need} so the door of the next run opens clear of it.
prob.cab.overlap: {a} hangs in the same place as the tall cabinet {b}.
prob.cab.wall-clearance: {no} hangs {clear} above the base cabinets; less than {min} leaves no room to work.
prob.run.over: Run {run} is {over} too long for its wall ({row}).
prob.run.gap: Run {run} leaves {gap} of its wall empty ({row}).
prob.filler.thin: Filler {no} is only {w} wide: too thin to cut and fit.
prob.filler.wide: Filler {no} is {w} wide; over {max} a cabinet looks better than a filler.
prob.counter.long: Countertop {no} is {len} long; a slab over {max} needs a joint.
prob.ff.opening: {no} has a face-frame opening of only {w}.
prob.nest.unplaced: Part {id} ({name}, {material}) does not fit on its sheet.
prob.est.placeholder: {n} of {of} rates in the cost estimate are still placeholders. Put in your shop's own.
cost.allplaceholder: Every rate here is a PLACEHOLDER: a round number, not a price list. Put in your shop's own rates before you quote anything.
cost.someplaceholder: {n} of {of} lines still use a placeholder rate (marked *). Put in your shop's own for those.
cost.area: Sheets estimated from the area of the parts. Nest the job in the Export view for the real count.
cost.csvnote: {n} of {of} rates are placeholders until the shop's own are set.
draw.save.set: Save all as a printable sheet set
draw.note: Drawings come from the same cabinets as the cut list, so they cannot disagree with it. Not to scale on the page: read the dimensions.
exp.nonest: Nest the job to get the sheet count, the cutting order on the labels, the sheets as a DXF and the G-code.
exp.gcode.note: One program per sheet of each material, made by PartCraft's nested-sheets path: contour cuts around every part with the tool you name. Not run on any machine.
exp.verify: Verify every file on your own machine and material before running it. Sizes are not tied to any maker's hardware: check before cutting.
label.title: Labels: {name}
csv.cut.name: Name
csv.drill.name: Name
msg.badfile: That file is not a CabinetCraft job.
msg.nested: Nested on {n} sheets; {u} parts did not fit.
sample.name: Example kitchen
room.intro: The room's outline (rectangle, L, U or a free outline with right angles), its doors and windows, and any island or peninsula. Cabinets are laid out along the walls in the Layout view and respect what is set here.
room.l.note: An L is the rectangle with a notch cut out of one corner. The walls become Wall 1, Wall 2 and so on, counter-clockwise.
room.u.note: A U is the rectangle with a notch cut out of the middle of one side.
room.free.note: One corner per line as x, y in {unit}, in order round the room. Every edge must run along x or y; edges may not cross.
room.free.bad: That outline cannot be used: every edge must run along x or y, no edges may cross, and it needs at least four corners.
room.pick: Pick the outline on the plan
room.pick.label: Plan to click the room's corners on
room.pick.note: Click the corners in order round the room. Each corner snaps to {grid} and to a straight line from the one before. Then Close outline.
room.pick.done: The room now has an outline of {n} corners.
room.reflex: starts at an inside corner (no wall behind its start)
open.gap.title: Puts a gap in the run's floor row where this opening is, so the cabinets after it move on.
open.note: A door is kept clear in front (and its swing is checked); a window may have a base cabinet below it but nothing in front of the glass. Checks flags what does not fit. Positions are measured along the wall from its start corner, the same way as the runs.
island.attach.start: Start end is against a wall
island.attach.end: Far end is against a wall
island.note: An island's cabinets stand on one side of its back line (the left as you go along it), with an optional second row facing the other way. An end against a wall makes it a peninsula: no end panel there, no overhang. Checks flags an aisle narrower than 900 mm (36 in), a common-practice figure, not a code.
island.layout.note: Island {id}: its place and size are set in the Room view. Its cabinets are laid out here like a run.
island.back.empty: No second row. Add cabinets here to put a row back to back, facing the other way.
cost.import.note: Download the rate sheet, fill in your own prices (a decimal point, not a comma), and import it again; or import a CSV (path,value) or JSON of your own. Only the rates you give are replaced; the rest stay marked as placeholders. The rates are saved with the job.
v3d.title: 3D in the PartCraft viewport
v3d.note: Places the cabinets as bodies in the viewport: a body for every panel, door, drawer front, filler, end panel and countertop, coloured by your material picks. One undo step; placing again replaces them. They are for looking at: not part of the part's solid, so they add nothing to its mass or an STL.
v3d.unavailable: This PartCraft cannot place bodies in the viewport (it needs add-on API 1.1).
v3d.room: Also show the floor and the walls (translucent, with the doors and windows)
v3d.none: Nothing of this job is in the viewport.
v3d.removed: The cabinets were taken out of the viewport.
v3d.label: CabinetCraft: place cabinets
exp.drillxml.note: A hole list per panel in a documented generic format. It is not any boring machine's own file format.
drillxml.note: Generic hole list per panel (cabinetcraft-holes 1). Not the file format of any boring machine.
cmd.cab3d: CAB3D: place the cabinets in the viewport
cmd.cab3d.clear: Take the cabinets out of the viewport
part.corner-bottom-b: Corner bottom, along the next wall
part.corner-top-b: Corner top, along the next wall
part.corner-shelf-b: Corner shelf, along the next wall
note.corner.triangle: Square blank: cut the triangle on the diagonal.
note.corner.round: Square blank: cut to a circle.
prob.cab.collide: {a} and {b} overlap on the floor plan by {by}.
prob.cab.outside: {no} does not fit inside the room's outline.
prob.cab.under-window: {no} hangs below {what}: a base cabinet or open wall is the usual choice there.
prob.corner.misplaced: {no} is a corner cabinet but is not the first or last item of a run that reaches a room corner, so it cannot turn the corner.
prob.corner.small: {no}: the corner cabinet is {w} wide and {d} deep, so each arm's door would be too narrow. It needs at least {min} wide.
prob.corner.double: {a} and {b} are both corner cabinets in the same room corner. Use one.
prob.island.aisle: Island {id} is only {gap} from {what}. A work aisle is usually at least {min}.
room.seg.note: Type the walls one a line, from the first corner: "length angle" for a straight wall (the angle is its direction in degrees, 0 = east, 90 = north), or "arc radius sweep heading" for an arc wall (sweep + bulges away from the room, - into it; heading is the direction from where it starts to where it ends). The outline closes by itself.
room.seg.apply: Make the room from these walls
room.seg.bad: Those walls cannot make a room: each line needs two numbers, an arc needs a radius and a sweep between 0.5 and 179 degrees, and the outline must not cross itself.
room.arcwall.note: Make one wall of a free outline an arc: pick the wall and its sweep in degrees (+ bulges away from the room, a bay; - bulges into it).
room.arc.bad: Those three points do not make an arc between 0.5 and 170 degrees.
room.pick.arc: Arc walls: click a point on the arc, then where it ends
room.pick.arc.mid: Click a point on the arc between the last corner and where it ends.
room.pick.arc.end: Now click where the arc ends.
rev.bay: bay: bulges away from the room
prob.corner.angle.angle: {no} ({form}) only fits a right-angled corner, and this corner is {inside} degrees inside. Use a diagonal-front corner cabinet (it is made at the true angle) or a plain cabinet with a closing panel.
prob.corner.angle.arc: {no} ({form}) is at a corner next to a curved wall: corner cabinets need two straight walls. It is laid out as a plain cabinet; use curved-wall cabinets along the curve.
prob.corner.angle.size: {no} ({form}) is too wide for a diagonal-front cabinet at this corner ({inside} degrees inside): its arms leave no room for the front. Make it narrower or shallower.
prob.corner.sharp: The corner between runs {a} and {b} is only {inside} degrees inside: no stock form fits (a cabinet end would stand across the next wall). Split the corner with a cabinet of your own design, or change the wall angle.
prob.corner.wedge: Corner {no} between runs {a} and {b} is {inside} degrees inside: the later run stops {stop} short and a closing panel ({no}) shuts the end of the other run; the dead corner behind it is a right triangle of {leg1} by {leg2}.
prob.corner.diag: {no} is a diagonal-front corner cabinet cut for a corner of {inside} degrees inside; its front is {front} long.
prob.corner.drillsize: Corner cabinets {list} are drilled where the system defines the holes; the sizes of {kinds} come from your own hardware and are still blank: type them in Export > Drilling sizes.
prob.arc.invalid: Run {run} stands on a curve of radius {r} that a cabinet there is too wide or too deep for.
prob.arc.over: Run {run} ({row}) goes {over} past the end of its curved wall: take a cabinet out or make one narrower.
prob.arc.gap.bay: Run {run} ({row}) on the bay (radius {r}): straight cabinets, each turned to the curve; the biggest gap between a cabinet's back and the wall is {gap} (in the middle of its back).
prob.arc.gap.bow: Run {run} ({row}) on the bow (radius {r}): straight cabinets, each turned to the curve; the biggest gap between a cabinet's back corner and the wall is {gap}.
prob.arc.void: Run {run} ({row}): {n} wedge-shaped voids behind the cabinets, up to {w} wide at the wall (hidden behind the fronts; the countertop covers them).
prob.arc.wedge: Run {run} ({row}): {n} wedge gaps between cabinets, up to {w} wide at the front: close them with wedge fillers or choose narrower cabinets.
prob.curved.straight: {no} is a curved-front cabinet but is not on a curved wall.
prob.curved.order: {no} has a curved front (front radius {r}, {arc} along the wall): it is made to order, so it has no cut list or drilling here and its cost is a placeholder until a maker quotes it.
note.corner.wedge: Closes the end of a run at a corner of another angle; the dead corner behind it is a right triangle of {leg1} by {leg2}.
note.corner.mitre: Mitred where the two arms meet: the cut makes {angle} degrees with the long edge (corner of {tau} degrees).
note.corner.triangle.angled: Triangle with a {apex} degree corner: cut it from the blank, on the diagonal.
note.corner.back.angled: Two backs that meet at {angle} degrees.
note.corner.door.angled: One diagonal door, {len} along the front.
cost.first.title: Type your shop's rates
cost.first.body: Every price here is a placeholder, not anyone's price list. Type your shop's own rates under Rates, or download the rate sheet, fill it in and import it. Until you do, the estimate is a draft.
cost.quote.draft: DRAFT estimate: it uses placeholder rates
cost.quote.final: FINAL QUOTE: every rate in use is your shop's own
cost.lint.open: {n} categories still use placeholder rates, so this cannot be called a final quote:
cost.lint.none: Every rate the job uses is your shop's own.
cost.lint.note: A rate counts as yours when you typed or imported it, even if it equals the placeholder.
hw.title: Drilling sizes you type
hw.note: Sizes your own hardware defines (dowel or cam fixings, a lazy susan's shaft and pivot). They stay blank until you type them; the corner cabinets' hole lists then carry them. Positions come from the 32 mm rules, never a made-up size.
dry.title: Dry run (checks the files, runs nothing)
dry.honest: No machine run has happened. This reads the programs and the hole list like a very small simulator and lists what it sees; the first real run on the machine and the maker's look are yours.
dry.rapid: Your machine's rapid rate (mm per minute), for the time estimate
dry.nofiles: No G-code yet: nest the sheets and make the G-code first. The hole list is checked anyway.
dry.summary: {moves} moves ({cuts} cutting, {arcs} arcs), {len} of cutting, tools {tools}, {changes} tool changes
dry.bbox: Reaches X {x0} to {x1}, Y {y0} to {y1}, Z {z0} to {z1}
dry.feeds: Feed rates from {min} to {max} per minute
dry.time.partial: About {cut} minutes of cutting plus {rapid} of rapid travel (type your rapid rate for a total)
dry.units: Units: the program says "{found}" and the job needs "{expected}".
dry.relative: The program uses relative moves; the checker reads absolute ones, so its numbers are not reliable.
dry.no-tool: No tool is selected before cutting.
dry.no-spindle: The spindle is never started before cutting.
dry.no-feed: {n} cutting moves have no feed rate.
dry.rapid-in-stock: {n} fast moves travel sideways while the tool is below the top of the sheet.
dry.outside: {n} cutting moves go outside the {w} by {h} sheet.
dry.outside-z: The deepest cut goes {over} below the bottom of the sheet (into the spoil board).
dry.deep: The deepest cut is {deepest} but the sheet is {t} thick: the parts would not cut through.
dry.hole.nopart: A hole belongs to part {id}, which is not in the cut list.
dry.hole.outside: {ref} ({kind}) at {x}, {y} is outside its panel of {l} by {w}.
dry.hole.edge: {ref} ({kind}) is {edge} from an edge; the drilling rules never go closer than {min}.
dry.hole.deep: {ref} ({kind}) is {depth} deep in a panel {t} thick.
dry.hole.blank: Holes whose size is blank (type it in Drilling sizes): {list}.
dry.holes.title: Hole list
dry.holes.summary: {holes} holes in {parts} panels, every one inside its panel; the rules keep the rim at least {rule} from an edge, the tightest is {tight}.
dry.mto: Made-to-order cabinets are not in the programs or the hole list.
run.notrun: No run has been made yet. This sheet is for the person who makes the first one.
run.dry.ok: {moves} moves, {len} of cutting, {min} minutes of cutting, no errors
run.dry.bad: {moves} moves, {len} of cutting: {issues} errors, do not run it yet
run.holes.ok: {n} holes in {parts} panels, all inside their panels
run.dry.note: The dry run reads the files only. It cannot see your machine, your clamps or your tool.
run.c.post: The post-processor matches this machine's controller.
run.c.units: The program's units match the machine's units.
run.c.tool: The tool in the spindle is the tool the program asks for (diameter, length).
run.c.spindle: The spindle speed in the program is right for this tool and material.
run.c.origin: The origin is set where the program expects it (front left corner, top of the sheet).
run.c.spoil: The spoil board is flat and the sheet will not be cut through into anything that matters.
run.c.hold: The sheet is held down (vacuum or clamps) clear of every toolpath.
run.c.limits: The program stays inside the machine's travel; the first move was checked in the air.
run.c.air: The program was run in the air, a little above the sheet, before cutting.
run.c.estop: Someone stands at the stop button for the first run.
run.f.cut: The first cut was watched from start to finish.
run.f.size: A finished part was measured against the cut list.
run.f.compare: The part was fitted against its neighbour.
run.f.sheet: The whole sheet was checked for parts that moved.
run.f.holes: The holes were checked against the hole list (if drilled on this machine).
rev.title: Maker's review sheet
rev.note: Every size and rule the corner cabinets, angled and curved walls and drilling used. Sizes are common practice and geometry, not any maker's hardware; no machine run or maker review has happened. Tick "maker confirms" or write the correction.
rev.src.rule: a rule of the 32 mm system (changeable under Materials)
rev.shelf.how: Pins in the end sides; the corner end of each shelf rests on its neighbour (maker to confirm)
rev.drill.pins: Pin rows: from edge / pitch / first hole
rev.drill.cup: Hinge cup: diameter, rim from the door edge
rev.wedge.legs: Dead corner behind it (right triangle legs)
rev.void: Widest void between cabinets, at the wall
rev.wedgefront: Widest wedge gap between cabinets, at the front
rev.none: This job has no corner cabinets, angled corners or curved walls.
@note.hosts: Keys of the host adapters are in lang-host/<app>.en.json (bim., cad., mod.); these are shared by every app.
hostroom.none: No room found. Select one first (see the note above).
hostroom.bad: This outline cannot be used as a room (it needs three or more corners and a surface).
hostroom.done: Room "{name}" taken from the model: {walls} walls, {placed} doors and windows placed, {skipped} left out (further than 600 mm from a wall).
exp.gcode.none: G-code: this app has no CAM export. You get the cut list, the nested sheets as DXF, the drilling lists and the labels (CSV, DXF, HTML); the DXF opens in PartCraft's Manufacture for G-code.
prob.host.nogcode: This app has no CAM export, so there is no G-code here: use the cut list, the nested sheets as DXF, the drilling lists and the labels, or open the DXF in PartCraft's Manufacture.
prob.host.snapshot: The cabinets in the model, building or drawing are made from the job when you press the button. Changing the job afterwards does not move them until you place or draw again, and editing them there does not change the job.
